description: Machine-readable inventory of agentic-setup audit checks for validation and generated maps.

statusTaxonomy.present: The expected invariant is fully satisfied.
statusTaxonomy.partial: Most signals resolve, with a small number of exceptions, or the project shows mixed adherence to a soft check.
statusTaxonomy.violation: Concrete content or configuration breaks the invariant.

relatedAudits.relationship: Owns human-facing documentation quality; instruction-file links to canonical docs overlap.
Owns application secret hygiene; settings-file secret checks overlap.

checks.title: Primary instruction file present
checks.expectation: At least one of CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, .cursorrules, or .cursor/rules/*.mdc exists at the repository root or an equivalent canonical path.
checks.violationSignal: No agentic instruction file at all.

checks.title: Primary instruction file is substantive
checks.expectation: The primary file is at least the minimum threshold lines and has identifiable structure beyond a single bullet list.
checks.violationSignal: The primary file is below the minimum-lines threshold.

checks.title: Primary instruction file is not bloated
checks.expectation: The primary file is at most the maximum threshold lines, because instruction files compete with the user's problem for tokens.
checks.violationSignal: The primary file is above the maximum-lines threshold.

checks.title: Project purpose documented
checks.expectation: The instruction file states what the project is and who it is for in identifiable prose.
checks.violationSignal: No purpose statement.

checks.title: Tech stack documented
checks.expectation: The instruction file names the primary framework, language, and runtime.
checks.violationSignal: No tech-stack signals at all.

checks.title: Architectural mental model documented
checks.expectation: The instruction file gives a brief architectural orientation: directory layout, dominant module pattern, or a link to ARCHITECTURE.md.
checks.violationSignal: No architectural orientation.

checks.title: Domain glossary present where appropriate
checks.expectation: When the project uses domain-specific terminology, the instruction file defines or links to a glossary.
checks.violationSignal: Heavy domain terminology with no glossary.

checks.title: Links to canonical human-facing docs
checks.expectation: The instruction file points the agent at the README, ARCHITECTURE.md, ADR directory, and CONTRIBUTING.md when those exist.
checks.violationSignal: None of the canonical docs are linked.

checks.title: Build, test, and run commands documented
checks.expectation: The instruction file lists the canonical install, dev-server, test, and build commands or links to a section that does.
checks.violationSignal: None of the four basic commands are documented.

checks.title: Code-style and naming conventions documented
checks.expectation: The instruction file states the project's naming, import-ordering, formatting, and abbreviations conventions.
checks.violationSignal: No conventions documented in a non-trivial codebase.

checks.title: Commit and branching conventions documented
checks.expectation: The instruction file states the commit-message convention, branch-naming convention, and any git add policy.
checks.violationSignal: No commit conventions in a project with multiple contributors.

checks.title: Testing philosophy or approach documented
checks.expectation: The instruction file states the testing convention: framework, query priority, behaviour-over-implementation, snapshot policy.
checks.violationSignal: Tests exist but no testing convention is documented.

checks.title: What to do and what NOT to do guidance present
checks.expectation: The instruction file contains explicit agent guidance: things to avoid and things to prefer.
checks.violationSignal: No agent-specific guidance at all.

checks.title: Tone or response-style guidance present
checks.expectation: When the project surfaces user-facing AI features, the instruction file documents the desired response style or persona.
checks.violationSignal: AI surface present with no response-style guidance.

checks.title: Imperative-present rule signal
checks.expectation: When the project requires Conventional Commits, the instruction file or a referenced doc demands the imperative-present subject form.
checks.violationSignal: Conventional Commits required but the imperative-present rule is not stated.
checks.skipWhenAbsent: Conventional Commits is not in use.

checks.title: settings.json is valid JSON
checks.expectation: When present, .claude/settings.json parses as JSON with no syntax errors.
checks.violationSignal: Parse error.

checks.title: settings.local.json is gitignored
checks.expectation: .gitignore excludes settings.local.json so personal overrides do not leak into the project.
checks.violationSignal: settings.local.json is committed or not gitignored.

checks.title: No secrets in settings.json
checks.expectation: The file contains no entries that look like API keys, tokens, passwords, or private URLs.
checks.violationSignal: A secret-shape or secret-named pattern match is found.

checks.title: No secrets in settings.local.json
checks.expectation: settings.local.json holds no secret-shaped values; secrets belong in environment variables and a secret manager.
checks.violationSignal: Pattern match in settings.local.json.

checks.title: Permissions are appropriately scoped
checks.expectation: The permissions.allow list does not contain more than the tolerated count of over-broad patterns.
checks.violationSignal: More than the threshold count of broad patterns such as Bash(*), Edit(*), or Write(*).

checks.title: permissions.deny is non-empty in security-sensitive projects
checks.expectation: When the project ships to production, permissions.deny explicitly forbids destructive commands.
checks.violationSignal: The deny list is empty in a deployed project.
checks.skipWhenAbsent: The project is library-only, or neither settings file exists.

checks.title: Hooks reference scripts that exist
checks.expectation: Every configured hook command is a one-line shell expression or invokes a script that exists in the repository.
checks.violationSignal: A hook references a missing script.

checks.title: Environment variables do not contain secrets
checks.expectation: The env block's values are not concrete secrets; secret-looking names are tolerated only with empty or referenced values.
checks.violationSignal: A concrete secret value in env.

checks.title: Status-line and model overrides are intentional
checks.expectation: When statusLine or model is set, the value matches a documented Claude Code option and is not a stale model identifier.
checks.violationSignal: A stale or invalid identifier.

checks.title: MCP-server entries are auditable
checks.expectation: Every mcpServers entry has a recognisable command, a transport, and either no secrets or environment-variable references for secrets.
checks.violationSignal: A concrete secret in an MCP-server config.

checks.title: Single source of truth for shared rules
checks.expectation: When more than one instruction file exists, one is the source of truth and the others reference it explicitly or are symlinks.
checks.violationSignal: Files contain conflicting guidance.

checks.title: Tech-stack mentions match dependencies
checks.expectation: Frameworks and tools named in instruction files appear in package.json.
checks.violationSignal: Multiple stale framework references.

checks.title: Commands documented match package.json scripts
checks.expectation: Commands shown in instruction files reference scripts that exist in package.json.
checks.violationSignal: An instruction-file command references a missing script.

checks.title: Cross-references resolve
checks.expectation: Internal references in instruction files point at files or directories that exist.
checks.violationSignal: A referenced file is missing.

checks.title: No retired-model identifiers
checks.expectation: Instruction files do not mention model IDs that have been retired.
checks.violationSignal: Multiple retired-model mentions in active guidance.

checks.title: Instruction-file freshness
checks.expectation: When the project has had recent activity, at least one instruction file has been modified within the freshness threshold.
checks.violationSignal: All instruction files older than the threshold in an active project.

checks.title: No abbreviations in agentic prose when the project requires it
checks.expectation: When a rule file declares a no-abbreviations policy, the instruction files comply with it.
checks.violationSignal: The policy is declared and the file violates it.
